newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia will not levy heavy fuel oil export duty.
newsitem.headline: Russia will not levy heavy fuel oil export duty.

text.p: Russia will not levy a duty on heavy fuel oil exports over this cold season, after the Fuel and Energy Ministry failed to find government support for its plan for a curb, officials at state oil firm Rosneft said on Friday.
"They (the government) have decided not to introduce any restrictions," Rosneft's chief spokesman, Vladimir Tumarkin, said.
Gennady Grigoryev, deputy head of Rosneft's financial-commercial directorate, which deals with export questions, said the same thing.
"It is safe to say there will be no duty. It's too late. We had all expected one, but it has not come."
Employees at First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Viktor Ott's office referred questions on mazut export curbs to Rosneft, the state oil holding firm which is being privatised.
"In November 1996, the ministry indeed proposed to the government a seasonal excise duty on mazut exports," Tumarkin said. "The ministry had the thesis that supplies should remain in Russia.
"But people dealing with this issue (in the government) remained silent, and decided not to introduce any restrictions."
Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said at a news conference on December 27 that Russia was preparing to introduce an export duty on mazut.
He also told Reuters last September that a duty would be levied.
Russian government officials wrangled for months over whether to impose a duty. The matter was and is shrouded in secrecy and has spurred many market rumours.

Russia raised the export tariff on mazut to 16 Ecus per tonne from six Ecus during December 1995 to March 1996 to curb deliveries abroad. It banned mazut exports from December 1994 to April 1995 to bolster supplies at home during the colder season.
